# Purpose

These sessions are a **hands-on data management plan (DMP) workshop**. Doctoral students organise a project folder and write the documentation that goes with it for **their own PhD project**, then transfer that text into the course assignment's Swedish Research Council DMP template.

The success criterion is the **5-year test**: someone returning to the project in five years — the student themselves or a colleague — can understand what was done and which decisions were made. This is deliberately methodology-agnostic; it must work for qualitative, survey, trial, and secondary-data projects alike.

Teaching time is **two afternoons of Team-Based Learning (3 h each)**, each preceded by a guided self-study morning (3 h). That is the constraint everything else is sized against.

# Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days, the student can:

1. **Structure** a durable project folder and write the accompanying documentation (README, decision log, naming and versioning conventions) so the project passes the 5-year test.
2. **Track** changes and decisions over time using **either** Git/GitHub **or** a dated decision log — and justify which track fits their project and skills.
3. **Draft** answers to the documentation, data description, and storage questions of the Swedish Research Council DMP template, using their own project package as the source.
4. **Judge** what can be shared, what must stay protected, and how to use KI-supported AI tools (Copilot-first) responsibly — including disclosure of AI use and verification of its output.

Outcomes 1–3 are assessed through the material students hand in; outcome 4 through peer critique and a short AI-use disclosure.

# What happens on each day

## Day 1 — Structure, documentation, and the 5-year test

| Block | Content |
|-------|---------|
| Morning (self-study, 3 h) | Orientation to the endpoint and the DMP assignment. Read a Good Enough Practices excerpt and the relevant KI documentation guidelines. Compare one good and one poor synthetic project folder. AI task: draft a candidate folder tree for your own project and keep the prompt and output. |
| Afternoon (TBL, 3 h) | iRAT/tRAT on core concepts (raw vs derived data, README, decision log, ELN vs project folder). Short clarification. Team application exercise: design folder + README for one shared global-health vignette and draft bullets for the DMP documentation questions. Inter-team critique against the 5-year rubric. Exit ticket: one change you will make to your own project. |

## Day 2 — Tracking changes, AI-assisted documentation, DMP draft

| Block | Content |
|-------|---------|
| Morning (self-study, 3 h) | Choose your track: Git/GitHub basics **or** dated decision log with file-naming conventions. AI task: turn your notes into a README and decision log, then verify and edit. Paste draft text into the DMP template. Prepare your own project package for the afternoon. |
| Afternoon (TBL, 3 h) | iRAT/tRAT on versioning, collaboration, sharing boundaries, and AI disclosure. Team application exercise on the students' **own** project packages, strengthening the DMP draft sections. Peer review against the 5-year rubric. Closing synthesis: what belongs in the data collection protocol instead, plus where to get KI support afterwards. |

**Students hand in:** the project package (folder + documentation), a partial DMP covering at least data description, documentation/quality, and storage, and a short AI-use disclosure.

# Scope boundaries (the point of this lock)

**In scope:** folder structure, documentation, decision traceability, ethical sharing boundaries, responsible AI use, and the DMP sections these feed.

**Out of scope** — signpost only, do not build materials for:

- Programming and statistics teaching; scripted analysis pipelines; containers and workflow managers.
- Git depth beyond what one track of one morning supports (K8F6106 covers this properly).
- The **data collection protocol**, the assignment's second component; we only note where instruments and versions live.
- More than one shared vignette, minute-level facilitator scripts, polished video, and new TBL hosting infrastructure.

Anything not listed as in scope needs team agreement before work starts on it; changes to this brief are logged in [`DECISIONS.md`](../DECISIONS.md). The detail behind these choices — course-outcome mapping, the Session → DMP question map, tool comparisons, and the build backlog — stays in [`session-plan.qmd`](session-plan.qmd).
